sanskrit: tato 'haṃ bharataśreṣṭha vegavantaṃ mahābalam amuñcaṃ samare bāṇaṃ rāmāya hṛdayacchidam
english: Then, O best of the Bhāratas, in that battle I loosed against Rāma a swift and mighty arrow that would cleave his heart.

sanskrit: tato jagāma vasudhāṃ bāṇavegaprapīḍitaḥ jānubhyāṃ dhanur utsṛjya rāmo mohavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Then Rāma, sorely afflicted by the arrow's force, sank to the earth upon his knees, let his bow fall, and passed into a swoon.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin nipatite rāme bhūrisahasrade āvavrur jaladā vyoma kṣaranto rudhiraṃ bahu
english: And when Rāma, giver of many thousand gifts, had fallen, the rain-clouds veiled the sky, pouring down blood in abundance.

sanskrit: ulkāś ca śataśaḥ petuḥ sanirghātāḥ sakampanāḥ arkaṃ ca sahasā dīptaṃ svarbhānur abhisaṃvṛṇot
english: Meteors fell by the hundred, with thunderclaps and tremors, and Svarbhānu suddenly swallowed up the blazing sun.

sanskrit: vavuś ca vātāḥ paruṣāś calitā ca vasuṃdharā gṛdhrā baḍāś ca kaṅkāś ca paripetur mudā yutāḥ
english: Harsh winds blew, the earth itself shook, and vultures, baḍa-birds, and herons wheeled down, filled with glee.

sanskrit: dīptāyāṃ diśi gomāyur dāruṇaṃ muhur unnadat anāhatā dundubhayo vinedur bhṛśanisvanāḥ
english: In a quarter of the sky that blazed, a jackal howled grimly again and again, and kettledrums, untouched by any hand, resounded with a deafening din.

sanskrit: etad autpātikaṃ ghoram āsīd bharatasattama visaṃjñakalpe dharaṇīṃ gate rāme mahātmani
english: Such was the dreadful array of portents, O most excellent of the Bhāratas, when the great-souled Rāma, well-nigh senseless, had sunk to the ground.

sanskrit: tato ravir mandamarīcimaṇḍalo; jagāmāstaṃ pāṃsupuñjāvagāḍhaḥ niśā vyagāhat sukhaśītamārutā; tato yuddhaṃ pratyavahārayāvaḥ
english: Then the sun, its orb of rays grown dim and sunk deep within heaped clouds of dust, went down to its setting; night drew on with its pleasant, cooling breeze, and so we two withdrew from battle.

sanskrit: evaṃ rājann avahāro babhūva; tataḥ punar vimale 'bhūt sughoram kālyaṃ kālyaṃ viṃśatiṃ vai dināni; tathaiva cānyāni dināni trīṇi
english: Thus, O king, the withdrawal came about; and again at clear dawn the fearsome combat resumed, day after day for twenty days, and likewise for three days more.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'haṃ niśi rājendra praṇamya śirasā tadā brāhmaṇānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then in the night, O lord of kings, bowing my head, I paid homage in full to the brāhmaṇas, to the ancestors, and to the gods.

sanskrit: naktaṃcarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ rajanyāś ca viśāṃ pate śayanaṃ prāpya rahite manasā samacintayam
english: And to the beings that roam by night and to the Night herself, O lord of peoples; then, reaching my couch in solitude, I pondered within my mind.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena me yuddham idaṃ paramadāruṇam ahāni subahūny adya vartate sumahātyayam
english: This grievous combat of mine with the son of Jamadagni has gone on now for very many days, and it bears the gravest peril.

sanskrit: na ca rāmaṃ mahāvīryaṃ śaknomi raṇamūrdhani vijetuṃ samare vipraṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahābalam
english: And I am unable in the forefront of the fray to conquer Rāma of mighty valor, that brāhmaṇa son of Jamadagni, vast in strength.

sanskrit: yadi śakyo mayā jetuṃ jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān daivatāni prasannāni darśayantu niśāṃ mama
english: If the resplendent son of Jamadagni can be vanquished by me, let the gracious gods reveal it to me this night.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ niśi rājendra prasuptaḥ śaravikṣataḥ dakṣiṇenaiva pārśvena prabhātasamaye iva
english: Then in the night, O lord of kings, wounded by arrows, I fell asleep upon my right side, as the hour of dawn drew near.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ vipramukhyais tair yair asmi patito rathāt utthāpito dhṛtaś caiva mā bhair iti ca sāntvitaḥ
english: Then by those very foremost of brāhmaṇas, by whom I had been raised when I fell from my chariot and upheld, I was comforted with the words, "Fear not."

sanskrit: ta eva māṃ mahārāja svapnadarśanam etya vai parivāryābruvan vākyaṃ tan nibodha kurūdvaha
english: Those same ones, O great king, came to me in a dream-vision, surrounded me, and spoke this word—mark it well, O scion of the Kurus.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha mā bhair gāṅgeya bhayaṃ te nāsti kiṃ cana rakṣāmahe naravyāghra svaśarīraṃ hi no bhavān
english: "Arise, fear not, O son of Gaṅgā; there is no danger whatsoever for you. We guard you, O tiger among men, for you are to us as our own body."

sanskrit: na tvāṃ rāmo raṇe jetā jāmadagnyaḥ kathaṃ cana tvam eva samare rāmaṃ vijetā bharatarṣabha
english: "Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, shall in no way conquer you in battle; it is you who shall vanquish Rāma in the fray, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: idam astraṃ sudayitaṃ pratyabhijñāsyate bhavān viditaṃ hi tavāpy etat pūrvasmin dehadhāraṇe
english: "This well-beloved weapon you shall recognize anew, for it was known to you as well in your former bearing of a body."

sanskrit: prājāpatyaṃ viśvakṛtaṃ prasvāpaṃ nāma bhārata na hīdaṃ veda rāmo 'pi pṛthivyāṃ vā pumān kva cit
english: "It is the weapon of Prajāpati, fashioned by Viśvakarman, called Prasvāpa, the Inducer of Sleep, O Bhārata; not even Rāma knows it, nor any man anywhere upon the earth."

sanskrit: tat smarasva mahābāho bhṛśaṃ saṃyojayasva ca na ca rāmaḥ kṣayaṃ gantā tenāstreṇa narādhipa
english: "Call it to mind, O mighty-armed one, and fix it firmly to your bow; nor shall Rāma meet his end by that weapon, O ruler of men."

sanskrit: enasā ca na yogaṃ tvaṃ prāpsyase jātu mānada svapsyate jāmadagnyo 'sau tvadbāṇabalapīḍitaḥ
english: "Nor shall you ever incur any sin thereby, O giver of honor; the son of Jamadagni, oppressed by the force of your shaft, shall but fall asleep."

sanskrit: tato jitvā tvam evainaṃ punar utthāpayiṣyasi astreṇa dayitenājau bhīṣma saṃbodhanena vai
english: "Then, having vanquished him, you yourself shall raise him up again in the fray, O Bhīṣma, by the cherished weapon of Awakening."

sanskrit: evaṃ kuruṣva kauravya prabhāte ratham āsthitaḥ prasuptaṃ vā mṛtaṃ vāpi tulyaṃ manyāmahe vayam
english: "Do thus, O Kaurava, mounting your chariot at dawn; whether a man lie sleeping or dead, we deem the two to be alike."

sanskrit: na ca rāmeṇa martavyaṃ kadā cid api pārthiva tataḥ samutpannam idaṃ prasvāpaṃ yujyatām iti
english: "And Rāma must never die, O king; therefore let this Prasvāpa, which has now arisen to you, be put to use."

sanskrit: ity uktvāntarhitā rājan sarva eva dvijottamāḥ aṣṭau sadṛśarūpās te sarve bhāsvaramūrtayaḥ
english: Having so spoken, O king, those most excellent of the twice-born vanished, all eight of them alike in form, all of radiant aspect.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ pratibuddho 'smi bhārata taṃ ca saṃcintya vai svapnam avāpaṃ harṣam uttamam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, when the night had passed, I awoke, O Bhārata; and recalling that dream, I was filled with the highest joy.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ mama tasya ca bhārata tumulaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ lomaharṣaṇam adbhutam
english: Then the battle began between him and me, O Bhārata—tumultuous, marvelous, and making the hair of all beings stand on end.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vavarṣa mayi bhārgavaḥ nyavārayam ahaṃ taṃ ca śarajālena bhārata
english: Then the Bhārgava rained upon me a downpour made of arrows, and I warded it off with a net of shafts, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddhaḥ punar eva mahātapāḥ hyastanenaiva kopena śaktiṃ vai prāhiṇon mayi
english: Then that great ascetic, wrought to the height of fury, with the same wrath as the day before, hurled a spear at me.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamasparśāṃ yamadaṇḍopamaprabhām jvalantīm agnivat saṃkhye lelihānāṃ samantataḥ
english: Its touch was like the thunderbolt of Indra, its splendor like the rod of Yama, blazing like fire in the fight and licking out flames on every side.

sanskrit: tato bharataśārdūla dhiṣṇyam ākāśagaṃ yathā sā mām abhyahanat tūrṇam aṃsadeśe ca bhārata
english: Then, O tiger of the Bhāratas, like a blazing meteor coursing through the sky, that spear struck me swiftly upon the region of the shoulder, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāsṛṅ me 'sravad ghoraṃ girer gairikadhātuvat rāmeṇa sumahābāho kṣatasya kṣatajekṣaṇa
english: Then my blood flowed dreadfully, like the red-ochre ore from a mountainside, O mighty-armed one, where Rāma had wounded me, O you whose eyes are red as blood.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ jāmadagnyāya bhṛśaṃ krodhasamanvitaḥ preṣayaṃ mṛtyusaṃkāśaṃ bāṇaṃ sarpaviṣopamam
english: Then I, filled with vehement wrath, sent against the son of Jamadagni an arrow that resembled death itself and was like the venom of a serpent.

sanskrit: sa tenābhihato vīro lalāṭe dvijasattamaḥ aśobhata mahārāja saśṛṅga iva parvataḥ
english: Struck thereby upon the forehead, that heroic and most excellent of the twice-born shone, O great king, like a mountain crowned with a peak.

sanskrit: sa saṃrabdhaḥ samāvṛtya bāṇaṃ kālāntakopamam saṃdadhe balavat kṛṣya ghoraṃ śatrunibarhaṇam
english: In fury he rounded upon me, and drawing back with might a dreadful arrow, the destroyer of foes, like Time the all-ending, he fitted it to his bow.

sanskrit: sa vakṣasi papātograḥ śaro vyāla iva śvasan mahīṃ rājaṃs tataś cāham agacchaṃ rudhirāvilaḥ
english: That fierce shaft fell upon my breast, hissing like a serpent; and then, O king, I sank to the earth, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: avāpya tu punaḥ saṃjñāṃ jāmadagnyāya dhīmate prāhiṇvaṃ vimalāṃ śaktiṃ jvalantīm aśanīm iva
english: But regaining my senses once more, I hurled at the wise son of Jamadagni a gleaming spear, blazing like the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sā tasya dvijamukhyasya nipapāta bhujāntare vihvalaś cābhavad rājan vepathuś cainam āviśat
english: It fell upon the shoulder of that foremost of the twice-born; he grew faint, O king, and a trembling came over him.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ pariṣvajya sakhā vipro mahātapāḥ akṛtavraṇaḥ śubhair vākyair āśvāsayad anekadhā
english: Then his friend, the brāhmaṇa Akṛtavraṇa, great in austerity, embraced him and comforted him in many ways with gracious words.

sanskrit: samāśvastas tadā rāmaḥ krodhāmarṣasamanvitaḥ prāduścakre tadā brāhmaṃ paramāstraṃ mahāvrataḥ
english: Then Rāma, recovered and filled with wrath and indignation, that hero of mighty vows, brought forth the supreme Brāhma weapon.

sanskrit: tatas tatpratighātārthaṃ brāhmam evāstram uttamam mayā prayuktaṃ jajvāla yugāntam iva darśayat
english: Then, to counter it, the same most excellent Brāhma weapon, loosed by me, blazed forth, showing as it were the end of an age.

sanskrit: tayor brahmāstrayor āsīd antarā vai samāgamaḥ asaṃprāpyaiva rāmaṃ ca māṃ ca bhāratasattama
english: Between those two Brahmā weapons there came a clash in mid-course, before either could reach Rāma or me, O most excellent of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato vyomni prādurabhūt teja eva hi kevalam bhūtāni caiva sarvāṇi jagmur ārtiṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Then in the sky there appeared nothing but a sheer blaze of fire, and all beings fell into anguish, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca sagandharvā devatāś caiva bhārata saṃtāpaṃ paramaṃ jagmur astratejobhipīḍitāḥ
english: The seers, together with the gandharvas and the gods, O Bhārata, fell into the utmost torment, oppressed by the fiery splendor of those weapons.

sanskrit: tataś cacāla pṛthivī saparvatavanadrumā saṃtaptāni ca bhūtāni viṣādaṃ jagmur uttamam
english: Then the earth, with its mountains, forests, and trees, trembled, and the scorched creatures fell into the deepest despair.

sanskrit: prajajvāla nabho rājan dhūmāyante diśo daśa na sthātum antarikṣe ca śekur ākāśagās tadā
english: The firmament blazed, O king, and the ten quarters were wreathed in smoke; nor could the beings that course the heavens hold their place in the sky.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛte loke sadevāsurarākṣase idam antaram ity eva yoktukāmo 'smi bhārata
english: Then, while the world with its gods, asuras, and rākṣasas cried out in dismay, I, thinking, "This is the moment," resolved to employ the weapon, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prasvāpam astraṃ dayitaṃ vacanād brahmavādinām cintitaṃ ca tad astraṃ me manasi pratyabhāt tadā
english: The cherished Prasvāpa weapon, by the word of those expounders of the Veda; and that weapon, when I called it to mind, shone forth within my thought.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato halahalāśabdo divi rājan mahān abhūt prasvāpaṃ bhīṣma mā srākṣīr iti kauravanandana
english: Bhīṣma said: Then a great clamor of "Halā! Halā!" arose in the heavens, O king: "Bhīṣma, loose not the Prasvāpa!"—so it cried, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ayuñjam eva caivāhaṃ tad astraṃ bhṛgunandane prasvāpaṃ māṃ prayuñjānaṃ nārado vākyam abravīt
english: Yet I was fixing that weapon upon the descendant of Bhṛgu; and as I was setting the Prasvāpa, Nārada spoke these words to me.

sanskrit: ete viyati kauravya divi devagaṇāḥ sthitāḥ te tvāṃ nivārayanty adya prasvāpaṃ mā prayojaya
english: "Behold, O Kaurava, the hosts of the gods stand yonder in the sky; they restrain you this day—do not employ the Prasvāpa."

sanskrit: rāmas tapasvī brahmaṇyo brāhmaṇaś ca guruś ca te tasyāvamānaṃ kauravya mā sma kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "Rāma is an ascetic, devoted to the brāhmaṇas, himself a brāhmaṇa, and your preceptor; do him no dishonor in any way, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ diviṣṭhān vai tān aṣṭau brahmavādinaḥ te māṃ smayanto rājendra śanakair idam abruvan
english: Then I beheld those eight expounders of the Veda standing in the heavens; smiling upon me, O lord of kings, they gently spoke this word.

sanskrit: yathāha bharataśreṣṭha nāradas tat tathā kuru etad dhi paramaṃ śreyo lokānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: "As Nārada bids you, O best of the Bhāratas, so do; for this is the highest good of the worlds, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: tataś ca pratisaṃhṛtya tad astraṃ svāpanaṃ mṛdhe brahmāstraṃ dīpayāṃ cakre tasmin yudhi yathāvidhi
english: Then, withdrawing that sleep-bringing weapon in the fray, I kindled forth the Brahmā weapon in that battle, according to the rite.

sanskrit: tato rāmo ruṣito rājaputra; dṛṣṭvā tad astraṃ vinivartitaṃ vai jito 'smi bhīṣmeṇa sumandabuddhir; ity eva vākyaṃ sahasā vyamuñcat
english: Then Rāma, O prince, was enraged; seeing that weapon withdrawn, he suddenly let fall these words: "I, dull of wit, am conquered by Bhīṣma!"

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat pitaraṃ jāmadagnyaḥ; pitus tathā pitaraṃ tasya cānyam ta evainaṃ saṃparivārya tasthur; ūcuś cainaṃ sāntvapūrvaṃ tadānīm
english: Then the son of Jamadagni saw his father, and his father's father, and yet another beyond him; they stood encircling him and spoke to him then with words of comfort.

sanskrit: mā smaivaṃ sāhasaṃ vatsa punaḥ kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana bhīṣmeṇa saṃyugaṃ gantuṃ kṣatriyeṇa viśeṣataḥ
english: "Never again, dear child, commit such a rash deed in any way—to enter into combat with Bhīṣma, and a kṣatriya at that."

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya tu dharmo 'yaṃ yad yuddhaṃ bhṛgunandana svādhyāyo vratacaryā ca brāhmaṇānāṃ paraṃ dhanam
english: "For battle is the duty of a kṣatriya, O delight of the Bhṛgus; but the study of scripture and the practice of vows are the supreme wealth of brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: idaṃ nimitte kasmiṃś cid asmābhir upamantritam śastradhāraṇam atyugraṃ tac ca kāryaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: "For some particular cause this most fierce bearing of arms was once enjoined upon you by us, and that task you have indeed accomplished."

sanskrit: vatsa paryāptam etāvad bhīṣmeṇa saha saṃyuge vimardas te mahābāho vyapayāhi raṇād itaḥ
english: "Dear child, enough of this; your clash in combat with Bhīṣma is sufficient, O mighty-armed one—withdraw now from the battle here."

sanskrit: paryāptam etad bhadraṃ te tava kārmukadhāraṇam visarjayaitad durdharṣa tapas tapyasva bhārgava
english: "Enough is this bearing of the bow by you—blessings upon you; lay it aside, O unassailable one, and devote yourself to austerity, O Bhārgava."

sanskrit: eṣa bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo devaiḥ sarvair nivāritaḥ nivartasva raṇād asmād iti caiva pracoditaḥ
english: "This Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, has been restrained by all the gods, who urged him, 'Withdraw from this battle.'"

sanskrit: rāmeṇa saha mā yotsīr guruṇeti punaḥ punaḥ na hi rāmo raṇe jetuṃ tvayā nyāyyaḥ kurūdvaha mānaṃ kuruṣva gāṅgeya brāhmaṇasya raṇājire
english: "'Do not fight with Rāma, your preceptor,' they said again and again, 'for Rāma ought not in justice to be vanquished by you in battle, O scion of the Kurus; show honor, O son of Gaṅgā, to the brāhmaṇa upon the field of war.'"

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu guravas tubhyaṃ tatas tvāṃ vārayāmahe bhīṣmo vasūnām anyatamo diṣṭyā jīvasi putraka
english: "And we are your elders; therefore we restrain you. Bhīṣma is one among the Vasus; by good fortune you yet live, O little son."

sanskrit: gāṅgeyaḥ śaṃtanoḥ putro vasur eṣa mahāyaśāḥ kathaṃ tvayā raṇe jetuṃ rāma śakyo nivarta vai
english: "This son of Gaṅgā, the son of Śaṃtanu, is a Vasu of great renown; how could he be vanquished by you in battle, O Rāma? Withdraw, then."

sanskrit: arjunaḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaḥ puraṃdarasuto balī naraḥ prajāpatir vīraḥ pūrvadevaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: "Arjuna, the best of the Pāṇḍavas, the mighty son of Purandara—he is Nara, the heroic Prajāpati, the ancient god, the everlasting one."

sanskrit: savyasācīti vikhyātas triṣu lokeṣu vīryavān bhīṣmamṛtyur yathākālaṃ vihito vai svayaṃbhuvā
english: "Renowned through the three worlds as Savyasācin, valiant—he has been ordained by the Self-existent as the death of Bhīṣma when his time shall come."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa pitṛbhiḥ pitṝn rāmo 'bravīd idam nāhaṃ yudhi nivarteyam iti me vratam āhitam
english: Thus addressed by his forefathers, Rāma spoke this to them: "I will not turn back in battle—such is the vow I have laid upon myself."

sanskrit: na nivartitapūrvaṃ ca kadā cid raṇamūrdhani nivartyatām āpageyaḥ kāmaṃ yuddhāt pitāmahāḥ na tv ahaṃ vinivartiṣye yuddhād asmāt kathaṃ cana
english: "Never before have I turned back in the forefront of battle. Let the son of the river-goddess be turned from the fight if you will, O grandsires; but I shall in no way withdraw from this combat."

sanskrit: tatas te munayo rājann ṛcīkapramukhās tadā nāradenaiva sahitāḥ samāgamyedam abruvan
english: Then those sages, O king, with Ṛcīka at their head, together with Nārada, drew near and spoke this word.

sanskrit: nivartasva raṇāt tāta mānayasva dvijottamān nety avocam ahaṃ tāṃś ca kṣatradharmavyapekṣayā
english: "Withdraw from the battle, dear child; show honor to these most excellent of the twice-born." But I said "No" to them, out of regard for the duty of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: mama vratam idaṃ loke nāhaṃ yuddhāt kathaṃ cana vimukho vinivarteyaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'bhyāhataḥ śaraiḥ
english: "This is my vow before the world: never in any way will I turn my back upon battle and withdraw, to be struck with arrows from behind."

sanskrit: nāhaṃ lobhān na kārpaṇyān na bhayān nārthakāraṇāt tyajeyaṃ śāśvataṃ dharmam iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: "Not out of greed, not out of meanness, not out of fear, nor for any gain's sake would I forsake the eternal law—such is my settled resolve."

sanskrit: tatas te munayaḥ sarve nāradapramukhā nṛpa bhāgīrathī ca me mātā raṇamadhyaṃ prapedire
english: Then all those sages, with Nārada at their head, O king, and Bhāgīrathī, my mother, came into the midst of the battlefield.

sanskrit: tathaivāttaśaro dhanvī tathaiva dṛḍhaniścayaḥ sthito 'ham āhave yoddhuṃ tatas te rāmam abruvan sametya sahitā bhūyaḥ samare bhṛgunandanam
english: Still I stood, my arrow taken up, bow in hand, my resolve as firm as ever, ready to fight in the fray; then they, gathering together once more, spoke to Rāma, the descendant of Bhṛgu, upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: nāvanītaṃ hi hṛdayaṃ viprāṇāṃ śāmya bhārgava rāma rāma nivartasva yuddhād asmād dvijottama avadhyo hi tvayā bhīṣmas tvaṃ ca bhīṣmasya bhārgava
english: "The hearts of brāhmaṇas are soft as fresh butter; be at peace, O Bhārgava. Rāma, Rāma, withdraw from this battle, O best of the twice-born; for Bhīṣma is not to be slain by you, nor you by Bhīṣma, O Bhārgava."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantas te sarve pratirudhya raṇājiram nyāsayāṃ cakrire śastraṃ pitaro bhṛgunandanam
english: Speaking thus, all those forefathers barred the field of battle and made the descendant of Bhṛgu lay down his weapon.
